transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-02-10
- Start: 14:30 UTC
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Ava Singh (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (NovaPay Eng Mgr), Lena Wu (NovaPay ML), Carlos Ruiz (NovaPay SRE), Maya Johnson (NovaPay PM)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review last week's throughput runs, tune continuous batching and concurrency targets, and define next benchmark steps. Open items around queueing/backpressure and staging network limits.

Topics:
- Results from last throughput run (1/2/3 configs)
- Continuous batching tweaks and padding/sequence length distribution
- Concurrency targets vs latency SLOs
- Queueing and backpressure settings for hosted vs dedicated
- Next benchmark and artifacts to share

[00:00] Ava Singh: hey everyone, thanks for joining, well go over the throughput runs you ran in staging and then outline the next bench. Samir, you wanna kick off with high level how things looked on your side?
[00:18] Samir Patel: yeah sure, thanks Ava. overall the runs showed about 2200 reqs/min on the default config, with tail latency creeping up above 400ms when bursty traffic hit. we tried the batching patch Diego sent last week and that bumped throughput to ~3200 reqs/min, but saw some requests spike to 950ms, which is kind of concerning for our checkout path.
[00:41] Diego Martinez: mm-hmm, okay that's helpful. when you say "batching patch" do you mean the continuous batching enabled with 80ms max wait + dynamic pad?
[00:51] Lena Wu: yeah Diego, that's what we enabled. we set max_wait to 80 ms and target batch size 48, default quantization q4 was used. also sequence-length distribution was heavier than expected, more 700-900 token tails because some users send full transaction notes.
[01:12] Priya Rao: just to chime in, quantization can cause slight variance on per-token time, but the big lever is average sequence length + how KV cache is populated. long sequences reduce effective batch density.
[01:26] Carlos Ruiz: one note from infra: when bursts hit we also saw CPU on the routing service spike, and a few 502s in staging; might be network egress or our LB connection limits. so need to separate model-side latency vs routing-side queueing.
[01:40] Ava Singh: good, so there are two buckets: model throughput (batching/concurrency/kv) and infra queueing (LB, worker threads). Diego, do you have suggestions on tuning continuous batching to avoid those 950ms spikes?
[01:53] Diego Martinez: yeah, couple things. first, lower max_wait from 80ms -> 40ms for latency-sensitive route (checkout). second, set adaptive concurrency: keep token-level concurrency target lower for checkout, e.g., 4 concurrent requests per GPU, while letting bulk ingestion reach 12. and enable prefix/KV caching for customer metadata so repeated small requests don't re-run full context.
[02:17] Samir Patel: if we lower max_wait to 40ms won't throughput drop a lot? we worry about losing cost efficiency.
[02:24] Diego Martinez: yes there's a tradeoff. but the drop is predictable; our numbers show ~15-25% throughput reduction but tail latency improves by 40-60%. also you can route checkout traffic to dedicated pool with stricter SLOs, and route background jobs to hosted burst pool.
[02:41] Maya Johnson: could you explain routing? were on the free staging cluster; moving to dedicated is a product decision and cost question for finance.
[02:51] Ava Singh: quick primer — Redwood routing policies let you tag requests (route param) and we can map route -> pool. checkout route could go to a small dedicated pool (2 GPUs) for stable latency and the rest of traffic hits shared pool. well share cost estimates.
[03:08] Priya Rao: another tuning: use batch bucketing by seq length so short requests group together; that lets short ones get lower latency even with larger batch windows. Also consider dynamic pad to reduce wasted compute if you have spikes of long sequences.
[03:25] Lena Wu: we haven't bucketed much; our generator groups are naive. we can export sample distribution — well send that.
[03:32] Carlos Ruiz: infra question: Diego you mentioned backpressure? how would Redwood behave under heavy queueing, will it reject or slow down? we saw some 502s, need to understand degradation model.
[03:44] Diego Martinez: good question — we support a few policies: queue with max depth + early reject, or shed low-priority requests. for hosted we recommend soft queue + priority tagging; for dedicated you can set queue size to zero and rely on rate-limiter upstream to avoid queuing. we'll send recommended defaults.
[04:00] Samir Patel: ok got it. can you also clarify KG cache — you said prefix cache, is that safe for PII?
[04:08] Priya Rao: prefix/KV cache is configurable and can be disabled per-route. in Private/Dedicated mode you get more control and encryption; for hosted we do ephemeral caches and keys are not persisted to disk unless you opt-in. 
[04:20] Samir Patel: understood.

[04:25] (screen share: benchmark spreadsheet link shared)
[04:28] Ava Singh: sharing the benchmark sheet now — link: https://redwood.prod/bench/novapay-weekly-02-10 (note: internal link placeholder)
[04:35] Lena Wu: thanks, pulling it up. I see run A (default), run B (batching 80ms), run C (batching 80ms + pad). Which ran had concurrency set high?
[04:46] Diego Martinez: run C used concurrency 10 per GPU, run B used 6. run A was baseline 2. pore — oh sorry "pore" mis-transcription there.
[04:56] (laughter)
[05:00] Samir Patel: the key metric for us is 95th percentile under load for checkout requests < 300ms ideally. right now only baseline meets it under low load, but under burst we fail.
[05:12] Diego Martinez: plan then: 1) reduce max_wait to 40ms for checkout route + seq-length bucketing, 2) set concurrency target 4 for checkout, 3) experiment with small dedicated pool of 1-2 GPUs for checkout to absorb bursts. that should bring p95 down.
[05:27] Ava Singh: do you want Redwood to run that test in our env or do you prefer NovaPay run in your staging?
[05:33] Lena Wu: if Redwood runs it in your env its easier for us, but we prefer runs in our staging to validate network behavior. maybe both: Redwood to run controlled bench and NovaPay to replicate in staging.
[05:44] Diego Martinez: agree. we'll run a 2-hour controlled throughput with the new params and then hand you config to run in staging. we'll include a script for the sample traffic and a request distribution file.

[06:00] (discussion of metrics to capture)
[06:03] Priya Rao: capture per-route p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, queue depth, and thread pool CPU. also trace sample requests that hit redis/kv cache miss to see downstream effect.
[06:18] Carlos Ruiz: well add network metrics (egress throughput, LB conn counts) so we can correlate spikes.

[06:25] (15 min of technical detail glossed: Diego explains code flags)
[06:28] Diego Martinez: flags: --continuous-batching=true --max-wait-ms=40 --concurrency-target=4 --enable-bucket-by-length=true, dynamic_pad=true, kv-cache=true (kv-cache masked for pii). We'll provide a yaml with these.
[06:46] Lena Wu: quick clarifying q: do any of these require model change or recompile?
[06:49] Diego Martinez: no model recompile. these are runtime config knobs; quantization stays the same. only time you'd recompile is if you change kernel selection or move to a different hardware arch.
[06:58] Samir Patel: what about autoscaling? we had weird scaling thrash last week where nodes spun up then killed, causing short 500 spikes.
[07:08] Priya Rao: likely your autoscaler step down was too aggressive or healthchecks were flaky. we recommend smoothing scale-down to 5-10 minutes and use rolling health checks. Diego will include recommended policy.
[07:18] Carlos Ruiz: can you send us the exact healthcheck endpoints Redwood uses?
[07:21] Diego Martinez: yes, included in notes.

[07:25] (customer question about pricing)
[07:28] Maya Johnson: high level on cost: if we move checkout to dedicated 2 GPUs what's the expected delta?
[07:34] Ava Singh: Ill send an estimate but rough: dedicated small pool adds fixed monthly plus incremental per-token; with improved batching you may recoup some cost. well model it in the cost sheet.

[07:46] (wrap-up prep)
[07:50] Ava Singh: ok to recap - Redwood will run the controlled 2h bench with new config, send the yaml and scripts, NovaPay will run replication in staging and share logs. action items in the doc. any blockers?
[08:05] Samir Patel: none on our side. need to confirm staging LB limits which Carlos will check.
[08:10] Carlos Ruiz: noted.
[08:12] Lena Wu: one more ask — Diego, can you include a short note on how prefix cache affects consistency for user-specific metadata? we want to ensure no stale answers.
[08:22] Diego Martinez: yep will include.

[08:27] (closing)
[08:28] Ava Singh: great thanks everyone. Ill follow up with the config and cost estimate. Next sync set for 2027-02-15 to review results.
[08:36] Samir Patel: thanks all.
